classification.difficultyReason: Apply the vertical line test to supplied discrete, continuous and piecewise graphs, including open and closed endpoints.

content.prompt: Decide whether these relations show a function using the vertical line test.

spec.description: Discrete relation with numbered axes; origin O omitted by house convention. Coordinates reproduce the plotted positions, not extra printed givens.
spec.mathematics: Six points with distinct x-coordinates; x ticks 1–8 and y ticks 5–30.
spec.answerVisibility: Graph always visible; classification belongs only to answers.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one plotted point.

spec.description: Six separate points on numbered axes; origin O omitted by house convention.
spec.mathematics: Distinct inputs 1–6; repeated outputs do not violate the vertical line test.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one plotted point. Repeated outputs are allowed.

spec.description: Discrete graph retaining vertically aligned pairs at x=2 and x=4; origin O omitted by house convention.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical lines $x=2$ and $x=4$ each intersect two plotted points.

spec.description: Discrete graph with two points at x=2; origin O omitted by house convention.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=2$ intersects two plotted points.

spec.description: Rising straight line crossing the y-axis above the origin and the x-axis to its left; unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: Nonvertical straight line; plotted equation is a representative reconstruction of the unscaled source.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the straight line once.

spec.description: Upward parabola with vertex on the negative y-axis and arrows at its upper ends; unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: Single output for each x-coordinate; representative unscaled parabola.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the parabola at most once.

spec.description: Right-opening parabola, vertex left of the y-axis, symmetric about the x-axis, arrows on both branches.
spec.mathematics: Vertical lines to the right of the vertex meet both branches.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line to the right of the vertex intersects both branches.

spec.description: V-shaped graph with vertex on negative y-axis and no endpoint markers or continuation arrows.
spec.mathematics: Two straight arms form a single-valued relation.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the V-shaped graph at most once.

spec.description: Four unconnected points, including a vertically aligned pair in quadrant I; unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: The two right-hand points have the same input and different outputs.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line through the two right-hand points intersects both.

spec.description: Four unconnected points at distinct horizontal positions; unnumbered axes.
spec.mathematics: One point in quadrant II, one in quadrant III, and two in quadrant I with distinct x-coordinates.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects at most one plotted point.

spec.description: Increasing blue cubic-shaped curve through the origin, flattening there, with arrows at both ends.
spec.mathematics: Representative unscaled cubic with one output per input.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the curve once.

spec.description: Blue circle centred at the origin, radius 2; all four intercept values retained.
spec.mathematics: Circle x²+y²=4.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=0$ intersects the circle at two points.

spec.description: Increasing concave-down blue curve to the right of the y-axis, crossing the positive x-axis and continuing steeply down near the y-axis.
spec.mathematics: Representative unscaled logarithmic shape; no equation is supplied to students.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the curve at most once.

spec.description: Two blue upper rays meet at the origin; a narrow teardrop loop below the origin returns to it.
spec.mathematics: A vertical line through the loop meets the relation more than once.

answer.worked: Not a function: the y-axis intersects the graph at the origin and at the bottom of the loop.

spec.description: Blue descending-then-rising curve has a minimum left of the y-axis and joins a horizontal rightward ray above the x-axis.
spec.mathematics: Continuous single-valued piecewise graph; representative unscaled quadratic segment and horizontal ray.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the graph at most once, including where the curve joins the horizontal ray.

spec.description: Left semicircle with its endpoints on the y-axis; no endpoint markers.
spec.mathematics: Upper and lower branches share x-coordinates.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line through the interior of the semicircle intersects its upper and lower branches.

spec.description: Decreasing blue curve ends in a filled point on positive x-axis. An open point directly above it begins a horizontal rightward ray.
spec.mathematics: At the shared breakpoint only the lower endpoint is included.
spec.answerVisibility: Open/closed givens always visible; classification only in answers.

answer.worked: Function: each vertical line intersects at most once. At the breakpoint the upper circle is open, so only the lower filled point is included.

spec.description: Three horizontal blue pieces with matching open/closed breakpoints: low left ray open at y-axis; middle closed at y-axis and open at right; high ray closed above that right endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Exactly one included point at each breakpoint.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects one included point. At each breakpoint the open circle is excluded and the filled point is included.

spec.description: Two separate sideways branches with vertices at (-2,0) and (2,0), opening outward; arrows at all four ends.
spec.mathematics: Vertical lines beyond either vertex intersect a branch twice.

answer.worked: Not a function: a vertical line to the right of $x=2$ intersects the upper and lower portions of the right branch.

spec.description: Vertical blue line x=2 with arrows at both ends; 2 labelled below its x-axis intersection.

answer.worked: Not a function: the vertical line $x=2$ contains more than one point of the graph.

spec.description: Horizontal blue line y=-1 with arrows at both ends; -1 labelled beside the y-axis.

answer.worked: Function: every vertical line intersects the horizontal line exactly once.
